description:
A non-recursive caller is re-analyzed on every revision of a callee's
current return, instead of once the returns it reads are settled.

Reduced cases: `def main(), do: Enum.take([1, 2, 3], 2)` (AnalyzeActivation
130 runs / 41 subjects; 43 re-runs woken by callee ReturnType current, 22 by
InputDemand, 16 by Recursive); fixtures2/behavior/enum_take_drop_split.fz,
a straight-line main/0 of 72 dbg(Enum...) calls, analyzes main/0 48 times,
each woken by one callee's ReturnType revision.
Paper: main/0 is in no recursive component; each callee return it reads
settles independently of main/0. main/0 needs one analysis to discover its
callsites and one per change in the argument rows it hands to its callees;
its return is final once every callee return it reads is settled.

Constraint recorded from earlier work: reading settled facts across a
recursive group was tried and refuted (unsound, oscillates). The paper must
show why a caller OUTSIDE every recursive component of its callees differs,
and the reader must measure it, before any builder.

Acceptance: main/0 analyses in enum_take_drop_split match the paper; no pin
rises.
title: A non-recursive caller re-analyzes on every current callee return
